text: But without knowing the specific details of what would happen over the next 20 years, we envisaged that services like online collaboration, e-learning and high-definition entertainment would transform the way we live, work and play.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The NBN’s value was all the more apparent during COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Its buffer capacity enabled us to cater for increased network traffic from the surge in digital interactions, with the vast majority of us working or learning virtually from home at one point or another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This allowed us to maintain some continuity in the economic and social activity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It took nearly 20 years for us to realise the full potential of NBN.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: That same forward-looking perspective we adopted for the NBN underscored our more recent decision to build 5G standalone mobile networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We foresee many possibilities in 5G for businesses, workers and consumers as a result of faster speed, lower latency and higher device connection density compared to 4G.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We facilitated the early roll-out of 5G standalone networks by allocating spectrum for our telcos to build them while setting clear performance, coverage, security and resilience requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, IMDA has awarded new and innovative projects under its 5G Innovation Programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One such project is the Hyundai Motor Group Innovation Centre in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For workers, it reduces labour-intensive activity and minimises the safety risks they bear in manually transporting heavy material.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It also creates opportunities for them to take on higher value roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Hyundai Motor Group intends to hire robotics engineers, data analysts and process engineers for the ‘intelligent’ manufacturing facility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For consumers, the more agile manufacturing process allows for hyper-customisation of ‘built-to-order’ vehicles to cater to different needs and preferences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is Hyundai Motor Group’s first such facility in the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They have shared with us that beyond Singapore’s position as a manufacturing and logistics hub, the Government’s support for innovation and cutting-edge digital infrastructure make us an attractive investment location.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I look forward to the facility’s launch and the benefits that it will bring to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Much like the vehicle manufacturing example, this project will help to reduce manual labour by enabling operators to pilot multiple vessels from a command centre and thereby also allowing cleaning services companies to manage manpower constraints in the sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These use cases represent the initial fruits of our early investments in 5G.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Just as the full value of our investments in the NBN was realised over time, we can expect more applications of 5G in the coming years as the rollout is completed, the ecosystem matures and demand shifts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, we find ourselves having to consider similar bets to those we made for NBN and 5G, to ensure that our digital infrastructure stack is poised to power Singapore’s next bound of growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This infrastructure stack includes wired and wireless networks which together provide connectivity within Singapore, subsea cables that connect us to the rest of the world, data centres that store and compute data which enable digital services, digital utilities which are foundational digital services such as digital identity, e-payment and e-invoicing, document attestation and data exchanges, all of which enable citizens and businesses to transact seamlessly and securely in the digital economy and "physical-digital" infrastructure such as Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices that enable the exchange of data between physical objects and digital networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is important that we continue planning for all these components in a holistic way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, for IoT deployment to grow, there must be security and sufficient capacity in our broadband and mobile networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For users to experience seamless connectivity at home or on-the-go, the Wi-Fi and mobile speeds must be comparable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: When it comes to digital infrastructure, the whole can be greater than the sum of the parts, provided we plan well and coordinate properly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We need to make the different layers and different components of the infrastructure stack work well together to sing together as a chorus to maximise our investments in each component.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Digital Connectivity Blueprint that Minister Josephine Teo briefly mentioned is being developed with this idea as well as future needs in mind.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The blueprint will outline what is next for Singapore’s connectivity infrastructure, including the broadband, mobile and Wi-Fi networks that power our domestic connectivity and subsea cables that provide international connectivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The blueprint will also identify interconnections with other digital infrastructure components that complement this connectivity layer such as data centres and digital utilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These interconnections are vital to maximising the value of the infrastructure stack.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As Ms Tin Pei Ling noted, it is important that we partner with industry to chart this path.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The panel brings together industry and business leaders who will help us to understand and account for the wide range of perspectives in the evolving digital arena.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Collectively, the members bring to the table insights on technical and business viability, international competitiveness, as well as potential business and consumer demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Both Ms Jessica Tan and Ms Tin Pei Ling spoke about the importance of considering security and environmental sustainability as we plan for our future digital infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is in line with the approach that the Government will and has been taking.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The panel’s deliberations will be guided not just by economic imperatives but security, resilience, inclusion and sustainability too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our partnership with industry goes beyond the panel.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Also informing the blueprint are MCI’s engagements with the wider industry, including on the NBN.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ms Jessica Tan asked about our next steps to enhance the NBN.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The decision to upgrade the NBN was prompted by trends toward more content generation by end-users and immersive interactions between users in the digital space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These have the potential to transform sectors such as education and entertainment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We want to ensure that our infrastructure can support such bandwidth-intensive activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is a significant endeavour on a nationwide scale.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is important that we undertake it efficiently and in close partnership with the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Industry players generally recognise these trends, the bandwidth requirements they bring and the importance of planning ahead for our NBN infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: MCI and the advisory panel will continue to engage the wider industry on the upgrade approach and consider their feedback as we chart our way forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We want to understand how they can enhance Singapore's digital connectivity and generate economic and social benefits for us in the future, just as 5G is beginning to do so today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Such upstream investments include the Future Communications Connectivity Lab, a testbed which IMDA partnered the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) to launch in Singapore last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: A more familiar tech area to many would be Artificial Intelligence, or AI, especially with the AI-driven chatbot, ChatGPT, gaining attention for its ability to generate content from law essays to code.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: When employed effectively, AI brings benefits for businesses and individuals, such as increased efficiency through the automation of tasks and better decision-making through the provision of data-driven insights and predictions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Government has been steadily investing in AI research and innovation and Singapore today is ranked among the top 10 countries based on publications at AI conferences and our researchers are internationally recognised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, the researchers at AI Singapore's Speech Lab have significantly improved the accuracy of transcribing our Singaporean colloquial speech to English text, taking into account our unique accents, terms and mix of languages used.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The solution has been adopted by the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) for their hotline services, improving back-end case management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to support our public research institutions in attracting and nurturing talent to drive innovation across the value chain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These Investigatorships are targeted at top-tier AI researchers who, in the course of their research, can also mentor and groom other promising talent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Two, enhancing the links between our research institutions and businesses, so that we can translate the fruits of our research into competitive advantages for businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our grant calls under the Future Communications R&D Programme support translational research.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The aim is for these demand-led projects to generate products for the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And lastly, we are boosting cooperation with international partners to help sharpen our research and innovation efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As Minister Josephine Teo has emphasised, there must be safety and trust in the digital space for our businesses and people to feel confident tapping on new technologies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are, therefore, also supporting the industry to pursue research and innovation in cybersecurity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: An avenue through which the Cybersecurity Agency of Singapore does this is the Cybersecurity Industry Call for Innovation, or CyberCall.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One company that benefitted from CyberCall is MicroSec, which found a new way to secure low-powered IoT devices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Building the trust and safety necessary for innovation to thrive goes beyond cybersecurity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Users must be assured that businesses are employing technologies, such as AI, responsibly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Minister has outlined in her speech how MCI is supporting businesses in providing such an assurance to customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In addition to research into emerging technologies, there is research that contributes to knowledge and appreciation of our history and heritage, to inform who we are as a nation and a society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Government records are a key part of such research.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Pritam Singh asked if the Government is prepared to release classified information that has already been extended for research purposes, to all sitting Members of Parliament.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is with reference to his request to an agency where the information sought had yet to be transferred to the National Archives of Singapore (NAS) for preservation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is distinct from public archives that are public records, that have been transferred to NAS and can be requested for inspection by any person, for the purpose of reference or research as set out in section 18(2) of the National Library Board Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For records that remain classified and are not part of the public archives, agencies may grant access to specific information for specific purposes, such as to write a book, and subject to conditions, such as complying with the Official Secrets Act, and submitting the information to be quoted for vetting prior to release.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In this particular instance, the agency had allowed the researcher access to relevant information from the records, with the understanding that the researcher would only publish and cite specific information with the agency's permission.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As a matter of policy, the Government does provide researchers access to information for legitimate research purposes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But doing so, does not mean that the entire record has been declassified, nor that it is generally available to the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: If someone has a specific reason to access closed records, a request can be made, and the request will be assessed by the Government on its merits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: If Mr Singh would like more information on the background, thinking or the rationale behind a Government policy, there are several routes he can take.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One way is to approach the relevant Ministry to provide further details and a clarification.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In addition, Mr Singh and Members of this House also have the option to file a Parliamentary Question, and receive a formal reply from the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There is a separate process where Ministries and agencies transfer their classified records to the NAS for long-term preservation and declassification when it is in the public interest to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is pertinent to the question Ms He Ting Ru asked about making archival material more accessible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The NAS has been working with Government agencies to declassify and make available more Government records.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In one example, the Government had agreed to declassify and release documents in Dr Goh Keng Swee's famous "Albatross File".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is a file that Dr Goh Keng Swee kept in the run-up to Singapore's separation from Malaysia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The process of declassification began some time ago, and took some time, given the complexity of the material.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: A subset of the material was part of a public exhibition, and a larger set of declassified "Albatross" documents will be released in a book on Separation, to be published later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They will include cabinet papers and Dr Goh's notes of his conversations with Malaysian leaders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are committed to ensuring greater access to Government records, so that they can be a reference for the public to research and obtain information on Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Building our digital infrastructure and research and innovation capabilities are foundational to a vibrant digital future for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With these strong foundations, our businesses and people have the ingredients to generate new opportunities and enhance their competitive edge, which Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How will speak more about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I want to end by reiterating that our efforts to shape a bright digital future are premised on a very human objective, to improve the lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And with an eye to the future and close collaboration among all of us, I have every confidence that we can and will create a bright digital future for generations of Singaporeans to come.

speaker: Mr Deputy Chairman
text: Senior Minister of State Mr Tan Kiat How.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Going digital is no longer a "good to have" for our firms and workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To stay ahead of competition and meet the needs of their customers, our firms must go digital or risk being left behind.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But we are doing so from a position of strength.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ninety-three percent of our firms have adopted at least one digital solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Firms have improved their overall digital maturity over the years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: However, given the uncertain economic outlook and near-term cost pressures, firms – especially our SMEs – may be tempted to press the "pause button" on their digitalisation plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Firms may find it difficult to catch up later.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In fact, I encourage firms to press "fast forward", to deepen digital capabilities and sharpen their competitiveness during this period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms Jessica Tan, Ms Janet Ang and Mr Sharael Taha asked how we are helping our businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: First, putting in place an enabling digital ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Second, assisting our firms in staying cybersafe, even as they use digital solutions more intensively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are putting in place enablers at the national, sectoral and firm levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At the national level, we are scaling up the adoption of digital utilities, like PayNow and InvoiceNow, which are foundational services that support core business functions of our firms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We launched the InvoiceNow Transaction Bonus last November.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I encourage more firms to make full use of this bonus.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At the sectoral level, we launched 20 Industry Digital Plans, or IDPs, since 2017.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Eighty-five percent of SMEs told us that they registered time savings and 75% of them reduced their dependence on manual labour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I launched the refreshed Food Services IDP in November last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This year, we will refresh the Retail IDP, the Security IDP and launch the Legal sector IDP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Eric Chua and Mr Abdul Samad asked about helping the broader workforce keep up with technological changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I am glad to share that the refreshed IDPs contain an updated Digital Training Roadmap that will guide our SMEs to upskill their workers, to allow them to make full use of the digital solutions that they adopt.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At the firm level, we are helping SMEs with different levels of digital maturity, as noted by Mr Christopher de Souza.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Since the Chief Technology Officer-as-a-Service, or CTO-as-a-Service, platform was launched last year, we have steadily expanded the platform as a single touch-point for digitalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Today, CTO-as-a-Service provides SMEs with access to a wide range of pre-approved digital solutions, alongside IMDA's digital consultants and additional support by partners, such as SGTech, which was mentioned by Minister of State Low Yen Ling earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In total, more than 21,000 users have accessed CTO-as-a-Service to find appropriate resources to meet their needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: More than 900 firms have taken the next step to engage consultants to develop their digital roadmap.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: More than nine in 10 expressed satisfaction with the service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Cyber threats have increased and risk wiping out years of hard work in seconds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I am pleased to announce that we will help our SMEs to develop their cybersecurity health plans to safeguard against digital risks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This is the cybersecurity equivalent of staying healthy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Taking proactive steps to be "healthy", such as designing solutions to minimise the risks of cyber threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ensuring regular check-ups or monitoring across a firm’s digital systems so that early actions can be taken.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Through the CTO-as-a-Service platform, SMEs can now engage cybersecurity consultants as "Chief Information Security Officers" (CISOs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These CISOs will work with the SMEs to develop tailored cybersecurity health plans based on the firm's risk profile and risk appetite.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Building on this foundation, MCI will develop the Digital Enterprise Blueprint to bring these efforts together in a comprehensive roadmap which will chart the next bound effort for our Digital Economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will be consulting industry leaders, associations, companies, unions and other stakeholders across different sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Their continued support and partnership will be crucial.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: (In Mandarin):   During COVID-19, many bosses of SMEs have experienced the benefits of digitalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Government will continue to work with our SMEs in their digitalisation journey, especially through schemes such as the SME Go Digital and Hawkers Go Digital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: However, I have heard that due to uncertain economic outlook and rising costs, some bosses are thinking of slowing down the pace of digitalisation transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: While I understand their concerns, I urge them to think twice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This is because digitalisation is like going against the flow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: If you do not move forward, you will be left behind.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As businesses all around the world are digitalised rapidly, if we stop for a while, we risk being overtaken by our competitors and even replaced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: (In English): We are committed to helping Singaporeans access exciting opportunities in the digital economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Before I elaborate on our plans, let me address the points raised by Mr Sharael Taha on the recent tech lay-offs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As a major tech hub, Singapore has been impacted too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But we have fared better than many parts of the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Southeast Asia continues to be an important market for tech companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These firms have long-term plans to scale up their presence here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Singapore has done well to capture this growth, anchoring these companies and their higher value tech development and corporate functions here in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These roles are often considered core to the companies' business and are more resilient to broad-based headcount rationalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, the average rate of re-entry into employment of retrenched residents for the I&C sector was higher than the overall economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Indeed, the I&C sector is one of our fastest growing sectors in our economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Our local workforce, in particular, has increased by 42% within these past five years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The increasing digitalisation across the economy has also contributed to healthy demand for tech manpower.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Locals account for more than 70% of overall tech jobs in Singapore, both the tech sectors as well as non-tech sectors.Today, locals in tech jobs earn 65% above the national median wage with good wage growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE)'s recent survey showed that Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) graduates from ICT courses have higher starting median pay compared to their peers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We believe the long-term prospects for our tech workforce remains strong and we will continue to support Singaporeans in accessing these opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But the tech space is a fast moving one and there are many competitors to Singapore's tech hub status.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We need to help our tech workforce stay competitive and relevant for the needs of tomorrow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: First, how we are working closely with industry partners to identify jobs that may be disrupted or emerging new tech roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: On the first aspect, the I&C Jobs Transformation Map launched last year identifies the impact of emerging technological trends on the I&C workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Employers are guided to redesign jobs, and upskill or reskill their tech workforce, to access these emerging job roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: On our part, IMDA will appoint training partners to develop reskilling programmes for these areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: IMDA appointed the National University of Singapore (NUS) and Singapore Polytechnic (SP) to set up the 5G Academy together with telcos and other companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Since 2020, the 5G Academy has trained around 10,000 professionals, exceeding the initial target of 5,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: He is a product executive who joined Singtel in 2015.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Through the 5G Academy, he was able to gain relevant 5G and cyber security skills to future proof his career.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: He now leverages his skills to enhance the security and performance of Singtel's products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We all need to shift our mindset to support Singaporeans like Mr Najib to fully realise the potential.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: One study found that 38% of hirers expected applicants to have a Bachelor's Degree for an entry-level position.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Firms are missing out a good pool of capable tech talent at a time when there is a global shortage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Furthermore, success involves more than just academic qualifications, but it is the hard and soft skills, like technical skills, attitude at the workplace and the ability to work in teams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This is also aligned with our effort to strengthen the social compact.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We want to give every Singaporean the best chance to succeed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The TechSkills Accelerator for ITE and Polytechnics, or TIP Alliance, in short, brings together IHLs and industry partners to look beyond academic qualifications and focus on skills-based hiring.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: He initially studied information technology (IT) at ITE and then, later on cyber and digital security at Temasek Polytechnic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: He is now doing a work-study degree in Applied Computing at the Singapore Institute of Technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At every step, he is supported by his employer, NCS, as part of its Fusion programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The TIP Alliance will continue to create more pathways for others like Mr Ihsan, through internships, apprenticeships and other programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It can take many forms, but most commonly refers to the act of making misleading claims that products are more environmentally sound than they are.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This is fundamentally an issue of false and misleading claim by a firm on its product, for example, how effective the product or how safe the product is.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This is an area that the Government is concerned as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These issues are taken under the Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act or CPFTA in short.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The relevant authorities and Ministries will study these.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But let me speak from MCI's perspective since Mr Perera filed the cut with MCI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: So, the Code sets out how the advertising should be conducted but false claims or misleading claims of the product will be dealt with under the Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act Next, let me turn to the questions by Ms Janet Ang, Mr Leon Perera and Ms He Ting Ru who asked about Government advertising.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Government is not unique in spending on advertising to promote awareness to the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Many companies advertise to ensure that their brands reach their intended audiences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: However, unlike private companies which can choose their target segments for marketing, the Government has to ensure that our messages reach out to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Singapore public also expects the Government to do its utmost to reach them via the channels and languages which they are comfortable with, such as vernacular languages, including dialects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Many Singaporeans, like our parents' and grandparents' generation, do not speak English but they are just as Singaporeans as all of us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And we want to make sure that they fully benefit from all the Government programmes and initiatives that we roll out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We use established industry metrics, including impressions, click-through rate, cost-per-click, and number of views for digital media advertising.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For print, radio and Free-to-Air television advertising, surveys are conducted to measure metrics like message recall.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This was necessary to keep the public informed on the pandemic crisis as it unfolded and the Government's responses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Respective Ministries are better placed to assess their advertising approach based on the outcomes that they seek to achieve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ministries have to rigorously evaluate their advertising budgets and be accountable for their programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In response to Ms He Ting Ru's point, advertising is typically part of a broader programme and effort by the Ministry and its outcomes should also be evaluated against whether those programmes and initiatives have met the needs or desired outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: That is how we should see the effectiveness of advertising campaigns, not just looking at the specific advertising programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In October 2018, MCI introduced a whole-of-Government demand aggregation contract for media buying for advertisement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This enhances value-for-money for the Government as a whole.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At the end of the day, Government's advertising spend is to ensure that all Singaporeans can make full use of the Government's many schemes and programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Perera referred to the Ministry of National Development (MND)'s print advertisement on accessible and affordable BTOs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms He Ting Ru also asked whether such ads are necessary and are they evaluated for effectiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: First, let me say that we appreciate that during this period, coming out of COVID-19, that Singaporeans are feeling anxious about the availability and affordability of BTOs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This information helps our Singaporeans make the best decision that they can and will reassure them that public housing is available and affordable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: There is no point made in the MND infographic to get Singaporeans to feel good about the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But it is the first time that I am being told that you feel good after looking at our MND infographic and I thank Mr Perera for feeling that way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I am sure my MND colleagues and HDB colleagues who are working very hard to make sure that they build BTO flats, clear the backlog, I think they appreciate it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: So, thank you very much for feeling good about it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ministries currently track the industry performance metrics to evaluate their campaigns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Additionally, MCI also requires Ministries to evaluate the effectiveness of their campaigns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: MCI does this for MCI-led advertisements, but MCI does not yet have a system to enable centralised tracking and we are exploring the best way to achieve it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Chairman, could I seek your indulgence for a few more minutes, please?

speaker: The Chairman
text: If you can keep it short, please, because there will be clarifications.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: COVID-19 has taught us that public communication is crucial to maintaining high public trust in the Government.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These made a difference to Singaporeans and we take this public trust seriously.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Mr Chairman, creating a bright digital future for Singapore is at the heart of MCI's work.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Minister Josephine Teo spoke about building a more inclusive and safer digital space for all.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary covered the next bound of our digital infrastructure, and research and innovation.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I touched on empowering our businesses and workforce to seize opportunities in the growing Digital Economy.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These efforts help us build a digital Singapore, where opportunities are open to all; where everyone can access basic needs and lead fulfilling and dignified lives – a home that we and our future generations can be proud of.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Together, I am confident that our efforts will enable Singaporeans to thrive in a digital future and take Singapore forward.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: The first one is related to human capital development.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: The scheme, such as Digital Home Access at Home, as well as the Three P events such as the DFL will go a long way in raising awareness and helping to propel population better for the digital future.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: But I would like to ask: what are some of the more proactive measures or programmes that may be put in place to help upskill our school-going children so that they can keep up with the rapid technological advancement and be ready for that digital future that we speak of?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: The second question, since we are talking about vernaculars, so allow me to speak in Mandarin.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: (In Mandarin):   I would like to ask the Minister this question: How does the Government ensure that spending on advertising and engaging influencers is meaningful, which will benefit the public, and is not for the purpose of self-commendation?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Are there any KPIs to ensure that the fund has achieved their intended purpose?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I will speak in Mandarin since she spoke in Mandarin.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Her online persona Ah Lian is very popular among the young.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Ah Lian’s friendly image has helped many government agencies to reach out to people who were hard to reach, reminding them to be vigilant against online scams.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: If they feel that the influencers are purely advocating for the Government, they would not be interested.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I thought that I will respond briefly to Ms Tin's question of what we are doing to help school-going children to acquire the digital skills.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If people are not able to acquire the skills that allow them to maximise the benefits of digital engagement, then it still does not go far enough.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have spent quite a lot of time talking about seniors.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With school-going children, there are two separate tracks of efforts that are proceeding in parallel.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are constantly looking at how its contents can be refreshed and made even more relevant, as well as broadening its coverage.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The other track of effort has to do with providing additional support for children from disadvantaged backgrounds.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For this purpose, we are very fortunate to have the support of our partners – through the DfL movement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Not only do these companies bring together their knowledge and understanding of how technology is changing our lives, they are usually also able to mobilise volunteers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Quite frequently, these volunteers are drawn from within their staff strength.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, these are two broad strands of efforts that are ongoing, and we will certainly continue to look at ways to strengthen them further.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Before that I also want to clarify that I did not feel good about —

speaker: The Chairman
text: I am sorry, Mr Perera, I cannot hear you.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I wanted to clarify that the ad did not necessarily make me feel good.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: In fact, I felt a little bit concerned for the reasons I shared in my speech.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: But my clarification is really going back to advertising that is driving behaviours amongst citizens versus advertising that is driving a belief or conviction.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: If you look at the ad that I showed earlier, the main aim seems to be to convince people that the Government is making housing affordable and accessible.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera

text: For example, if you have advertising to say, "Hey, you know" —

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Perera, if I could ask you to ask your clarification question concisely, please?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I think I will leave it at that.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Mr Chairman, let me just look at some of the ads and campaigns we have done during the COVID-19 pandemic – getting our seniors to go for their vaccination, telling people about the safe management protocols and so on.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Even some of our campaigns which some Singaporeans may think are a little bit cheesy, for example, being kind to one another, making sure that you prevent dengue by preventing mosquito breeding in our homes.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These are for making sure that Singaporeans understand the facts and make sure that we encourage good behaviour among Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I am not sure how Mr Perera thinks that it is not a good idea in getting more people to be kinder to another, to be more courteous to one another, to take care about the cleanliness and hygiene in our homes, to benefit our neighbours.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I really do not quite understand where Mr Perera is coming from.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These are just facts to help Singaporeans make the best decision for themselves.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And I am sure Singaporeans can do so.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: It will go some ways to encouraging SMEs to understand their cybersecurity risks because it will develop.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: There will be a health plan for the SMEs.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: But just like all health plans, the real benefit is when you do something about it after you get your health plan.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: So, can I ask the Senior Minister of State what more can we do to shift the mindset of SMEs who need to focus on some of the business challenges to also give that right emphasis to be looking at cybersecurity and making their companies safe so that they can be competitive?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Member for asking a very pertinent question.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Even as we support the digitalisation efforts of our SMEs, getting them to stay safe online is important consideration and priority.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: You might be a consequence of an attack.

text: Vulnerabilities exploited in one firm could affect many in the supply chain and many of their customer segments.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In addition to the cybersecurity health plan which I spoke about just now in my speech, the CSA has been working with industry associations and companies, on various efforts.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These are visible indicators for enterprises to demonstrate to their suppliers, to their customers, that they have a certain level of cybersecurity measures in place, which in turn gives their business partners and customers the confidence and trust to transact with them.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This enables enterprises to better differentiate themselves from other firms, their competitors and offering a competitive advantage ahead of their peers.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is an important point that I hope SMEs and firms can also consider.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It is also how you signal to your business partners and your customers that you are differentiated from the rest.

text: The release of these documents, legacy historical documents, are important for the nation as part of the nation-building process.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Particularly in the case of the Albatross Files, I think they will show, as I understand, that separation was negotiated over a number of months and it was not a case of Singapore being kicked out.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: At least, that is what one commentator shared on National Day last year in an article in TODAY newspaper.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I think the fundamental point is I think more of the release of such information is something that the good people at the National Archives should be acknowledged for.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Mr Pritam Singh will appreciate that whether something is in the public interest for general release, does not only relate to the content of the document.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It can also relates to the personnel that were involved in writing that document, managing the information, how that document relates to other material that is in the Archives or in other parts of the document store, as well as the process of that happening.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There is not a single template or algorithm to decide for all documents and it is done in conjunction with the Ministries and agencies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Pritam Singh and also appreciate his comments that the scheme is to be welcomed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The income criteria that is applicable, I think it is not directly comparable because it is a merger of two schemes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is to recognise the greater needs of such families.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: I want to thank the Minister and our two Senior Ministers of State.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: I also want to take this opportunity to thank the whole of MCI team.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: I hope that you are not affected by the comments made by certain Members, just now, at the COS.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Let us not forget the fact that during the COVID-19 period, the MCI team worked very hard around the clock to make sure that the correct and most accurate information is spread across the entire Singapore, uniting all Singaporeans to be together.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: I understand that in relation to the topic of scams, this was largely discussed during the MHA COS, but I also want to know how is MCI securing our communications channels to shield citizens from scams?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: The next question is given how technologies, which include the rise of online platforms, have disrupted the media industry worldwide, how is MCI helping our homegrown film and media companies to transform as well as to seize more new opportunities?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, firstly, I would like to thank Ms Hany Soh for her acknowledgement of my colleagues' efforts during the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think not only are they gratified, more importantly, they appreciate the fact that they were able to make a contribution to help Singapore through a very difficult period.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To your question on scams, you are right.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Minister of State Sun Xueling had covered it in fairly great detail during the COS debate for MHA yesterday.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: One of the things that she described was the multilayered approach that we take in fighting scams.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are interventions at the level of the individual.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are also interventions at the level of financial services – the banks, primarily.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Another very important layer that you described is intervention within the telco infrastructure.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This has been in place since last October.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Since this January, we have, of course, mandated the SMS Sender ID Registry for those that use alphanumeric headers for their SMSes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, that is something that has been worked on.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As was also mentioned in the media today, we are looking at whether an option can be made available to subscribers to decide that they do not want to be on the receiving end of overseas calls at all because the vast majority of scam calls originated from abroad.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In some instances, people know very well that they do not have an overseas network.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They have no reason to be receiving an overseas call.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In order to prevent themselves from falling victim, they would rather not receive these calls.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is an option that we are studying together with the telcos.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We hope to be able to update you soon.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: Just one clarification for Senior Minister of State Tan.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: I think he mentioned earlier that Government advertising schemes have to target everyone.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: It appears to me that this is a bit of a missed opportunity to be a bit more targeted and efficient in the spending that we do on our advertising.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: I think nobody here disagrees that for COVID-19, for example, we have to target the whole of nation and not just Singaporeans, but also people who live in our communities regardless of their citizenship status.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: The point that I was making is whether we can get better outcomes with the money that we spend.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: So, would MCI, for example, consider having more targeted advertisement – or rather not just MCI but all the Ministries in general – would they consider having more targeted advertising campaigns rather than take a very broad-stroke approach to ensure that we are just spending more wisely?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Ms He for her question and her suggestion.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Actually, we are on the same page on this.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: For us, we do want to get the maximum return on investment (ROI) on the marketing spend and the advertising spend – not just on advertising and marketing, but in general, from all Government expenditure.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Maybe just allow me to just elaborate on a couple of points that may be useful for Ms He.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is probably much lower than many private sector companies.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It would probably be above 5% of their total sales, for big companies.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We are not trying to be like the big MNCs or private sector companies, but it is a sanity check for us to say that we are not overspending.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: They will have to justify rigorously, evaluate the various options and justify those budgets internally.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I mentioned some just now for the digital media space, including impressions, clickthrough rates, cost per click, number of views and so on to measure how well those campaigns are doing.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, first and foremost, we are on the same page on this.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: That is something we will continue doing and I thank Ms He for her suggestion.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On whether MCI ought to look at this centrally and holistically, I mentioned in my earlier reply that we are indeed exploring ways to do so and we will consider how to do so effectively.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: That is something that we also try to do, targeting our campaign so that the messages reach the intended audience.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It is not just about a more efficient use of the advertising money, but also it is more important to reach out to segments of Singaporeans to inform them of specific set of considerations that they need to have or need to think about for that specific programme.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: For example, I go back to COVID-19 vaccination.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: How do we target to reach seniors, especially those who may not speak English, may not even speak Mandarin or the vernacular languages but in dialects?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Targeted advertising in a way that resonates with them – this is something we were looking at.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: But at the same time, we also have to balance between being very personal and targeted, with personal privacy.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I am sure Ms He and her colleagues have also due consideration of personal privacy and data protection.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We try to be targeted and personalised but at same time protecting the privacy of the person.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, it is a balance but I agree with Ms He that this is something that we are looking at.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling, would you like to withdraw the amendment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Was there one more question that was not answered?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Yes, there was one question that was not answered.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: This is in relation to the support for local companies.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Given how technology, which includes the rise of online platforms, has disrupted the media industry worldwide, how is MCI helping our homegrown film and media companies transform and seize more new opportunities?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In response to the question by the Member, indeed, we are supporting the global ambitions of our homegrown media companies, especially our homegrown media studios, by strengthening capabilities through close partnerships between them and the larger players in the industry like the MNCs and by encouraging them to adopt the latest technologies.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I think we are very proud of many of our "Made with Singapore" content, for example, the recent "Ajoomma".

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: As a next step, we will continue to strengthen this partnership between our media firms with global media studios.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We will support virtual production produced short-form content.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We are evaluating them and IMDA will announce the results soon.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We will also be launching a virtual production challenge, partnering with Epic Games.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Shortlisted participants will undergo Epic Games training with funds supporting production of narrative-based content using their real-time 3D content tool engine, the Unreal Engine.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We are working very closely with the media industry to create local intellectual property (IP) – "Made with Singapore" content that can travel to the rest of the world, helping our firms to use technology to produce content more efficiently and meet the more sophisticated needs of consumers around the world.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Tin, if you can withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I think, despite all the questions that have been asked, respect goes to all of you for being on the ground, in the trenches, facing off the challenges that you have to face and making that inclusive digital future a reality.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: With that, I would like to withdraw my amendment.
